cards.source: REF 5.1 (india_ideology.jpg) recovers the question and the answer 'No. Hit us first and you'll breathe your last.' on the SUPREMO side; the opposite side is authored here because only one face was ever legible. REF 2.4 records that zero ordinary question cards were recovered in full.
cards.question: Do you condemn the use of surgical strikes as a reactionary tool?

sides.answer: No. Hit us first and you'll breathe your last.
Yes. A people who cannot be reached by argument can be reached by theatre.

cards.source: REF 5.2 verifies the Capitalist side of the shipped 'SHOULD WE INVADE NEW SPAIN?' card pays 2 Trust + 1 Media and ZERO Funds, and REF 8.1 recovers the 'far more lucrative to invade nearby islands' answer. The Supremo side is authored; the ideologue of the recovered answer is inferred from its reasoning.
cards.question: Should we invade New Spain?

sides.answer: No. It would be far more lucrative to invade nearby islands and expand our fishing territories.
Yes. The strait was ours before it was theirs, and the story should say so.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 3, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Should mistakes be forgiven?

sides.answer: No. A queue that does not move is only a queue with better lighting.
Yes. Forgive the mistake, publish the method, and let the crowd do the arithmetic.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 4, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Should women be free to have children single or in a relationship?

sides.answer: Yes. The state has no standing in a bedroom.
No. The next decade is a budget line, and the budget line is not neutral.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 5, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Should the government spend money on space exploration?

sides.answer: Yes. Nothing on this surface has ever been solved by staying on it.
No. There is a bus stop on this planet that still has no roof.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 6, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Is providing free food, housing and healthcare to all citizens a good idea?

sides.answer: Yes. Give them the floor and they will build the walls themselves.
No. Free is not a policy. Free is a queue with a nicer name.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 7, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Do the poor have the right to take wealth from the rich?

sides.answer: No. Ownership is the only argument that has ever survived a recession.
Yes. The argument was never about ownership. It was about who was holding it.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 8, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Should the rich be taxed to fund free higher education?

sides.answer: Yes. A debt forgiven at eighteen is cheaper than a country that is not.
No. Every free seat is a private school with a public address.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2 (deadpan, Yes./No. opener, no jokes in the answer). Added because the recovered question pool is eight cards deep and one deck cannot show a fourth of the pairing table.
cards.question: Should the corporation fund the festival or should the festival fund the corporation?

sides.answer: No. Let them pay for the drums. The logo will still be on the stage.
Yes. Make them pay for the road as well. Roads are remembered longer than stages.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 2.3 infers from 14 tournament hands that Idealist and Supremo sit in largely disjoint question space; this card tests the seam rather than filling it.
cards.question: Should the spokesperson resign before the committee finishes reading?

sides.answer: No. Leaving now is a statement. Staying is a sentence.
Yes. Read the whole file before you answer any part of it.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Added to cover the Showstopper x Supremo pairing, which the recovered question pool never exercises.
cards.question: Should the broadcast continue while the repair crew is still in the room?

sides.answer: No. Show the room. The audience can decide for itself what a hole is worth.
Yes. Show the finished room. Nobody has ever voted for a half-built wall.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Added so the Capitalist x Supremo pair is not carried entirely by the two recovered New Spain / wealth answers.
cards.question: Should the old market stay open until the new one is finished?

sides.answer: No. The new market needs the old one's footfall for a year before it can stand.
Yes. A city that keeps both pays for both and decides about neither.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 3 (question at most 12 words, answer at most 15 after the Yes/No) is the authoring constraint here; the situation carries the satire and the wording stays flat.
cards.question: Should the tender be reopened every year or awarded once?

sides.answer: No. Award it once and the work is finished before anyone can challenge the price.
Yes. Reopen it every year and the price falls to the lowest bidder's comfort.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The recovered question pool contains no procurement question at all, which is the register's largest silence.
cards.question: Should a defaulting contractor be allowed to bid again?

sides.answer: No. A record of failure is the only collateral anyone has ever offered.
Yes. Ban them and the next contractor is worse, and the file says so.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the toll be raised to fund the bridge that replaced it?

sides.answer: Yes. The bridge is a longer-lived asset than the toll ever was.
No. The toll was the only part of that road anyone could point at.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should land records be digitised before the next election?

sides.answer: Yes. Digitise it now and the next sale is clean enough to tax.
No. Digitise it now and the next sale is fast enough to be invisible.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Welfare questions recovered at REF 8.1 items 6 and 8 are all-or-nothing; this one is about the boundary of a scheme that already exists.
cards.question: Should free bus travel be extended to the district?

sides.answer: No. Extend it and the ticket-holding commuters are paying for the rest.
Yes. Extend it and the road fills with people counted nowhere else.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the pension age rise with life expectancy?

sides.answer: No. Lower it instead and pay for it out of the same accounts.
Yes. Tie it to expectancy and the ledger finally means something.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the minister appear on the news every week?

sides.answer: No. Once a quarter is enough, and the audit confirms it either way.
Yes. Weekly is cheap, and nobody checks what was said by Tuesday.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 4 forbids a joke in the answer; the joke here is entirely in the situation.
cards.question: Should the press conference be streamed before it is edited?

sides.answer: No. Edit it first and the sentence survives the week.
Yes. Stream it raw and the clip does the work of a campaign.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the campaign advertise the number of schools opened?

sides.answer: No. Advertise the accounts and the schools will read the advertisement.
Yes. Advertise the number and the arithmetic waits for the next election.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the protest permit be decided by the court or the police?

sides.answer: No. By the court, and the refusal acquires a signature.
Yes. By the police, and the crowd still turns up on the day.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 8 permits references to real subjects; no individual is named, the question is the register's ordinary register of consequence rather than of person.
cards.question: Should a deserter's name be published after the war ends?

sides.answer: No. Publish it and the next recruitment is only a rumour.
Yes. Publish it and the next recruitment is at least accurate.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the minister's statements be archived with their dates?

sides.answer: No. Archive them and the ministry becomes a museum by Friday.
Yes. Archive them with dates and the archive becomes the story.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the opposition be given more time on the news?

sides.answer: No. Equal time and the argument stops being an argument.
Yes. More airtime and the argument survives the week.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the rally be allowed on the main road?

sides.answer: Yes. Allow it and the road learns what it is for.
No. Redirect it and the footage is better.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 7 requires campaign variety; this is the enumeration question the recovered pool never reaches.
cards.question: Should the census count the people who sleep in the district?

sides.answer: Yes. Count them where they sleep and the number is honest.
No. Count them where they vote and the number is convenient.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the free lunch continue through the summer holidays?

sides.answer: Yes. The building is empty and the kitchen is not.
No. End it in June and July stops being visible.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the examination results be published with the schools named?

sides.answer: Yes. Name the schools and the parents will actually read them.
No. Name the schools and the parents read nothing else.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2.
cards.question: Should the memorial be built where the crowd was standing?

sides.answer: Yes. Where they stood, so the ground keeps the argument.
No. Where it photographs cleanly, and the ground stays quiet.

cards.source: REF 8.1 item 9 recovers the stem 'SHOULD WE [STOP] AERIAL BOMBING DEVELOPED COUNTRIES?' legible in the official 432-card marketing render, but the verb is bracketed by the researcher as an inference and REF 8.1 says explicitly: do not treat as verbatim. MISSING CLAUSE: one word, the verb, which is supplied here. No answer side was legible at all; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Should we stop aerial bombing developed countries?

sides.answer: No. They are our largest export market and markets are not bombed.
Yes. Stop it and the footage stops being a reason to continue.

cards.source: REF 8.1 item 10 recovers the stem 'SHOULD KASHMIRI FARMERS BE GIVEN THE RIGHT TO FLY […]?' legible only up to the word FLY; REF 8.1 says explicitly: do not treat as verbatim. MISSING CLAUSE: the object of 'fly' — 'drones' is supplied here and is authored, not recovered. No answer side was legible at all; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register.
cards.question: Should Kashmiri farmers be given the right to fly drones?

sides.answer: No. Every licence issued is one more reason to withdraw it.
Yes. Issue it and watch who stops appearing at the border.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Authored to open the register's smallest scale. REF 2.3 infers the recovered question pool is entirely national and international in framing; no recovered card concerns a village panchayat, a water right or a local allocation, so the deck had no small-scale question at all.
cards.question: Should the panchayat's water allocation favour the fields that have always had water?

sides.answer: Yes. Every new borewell is a subsidy to whoever drilled deepest.
No. Entitlement is the only inheritance that does not need a lawyer.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. A creditor-versus-debtor question. The recovered pool contains one wealth question (REF 8.1 item 7) and one taxation question (item 8) and no question about who absorbs a loss already booked, which is a different trade.
cards.question: Should farm loan waivers be paid to the banks or to the farmers?

sides.answer: Yes. A bank that cannot lend stops lending to everyone.
No. The debt was raised at the farmer's table, not the bank's.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Authored to put the two sides on opposite sides of an international obligation, where the recovered pool's only non-domestic questions are about invading and bombing other countries.
cards.question: Should India pay more than its agreed share of the climate fund?

sides.answer: Yes. A payer in arrears loses the vote on where it is spent.
No. A share that grows with capacity is a share nobody signs.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Authored because the recovered welfare questions (REF 8.1 items 6 and 8) are all about whether a benefit exists, and none about who inside the household is measured by it. The Capitalist side is the restrained one here, which is the deck's answer to a greedy side reading as the obvious one.
cards.question: Should a working spouse's earnings count in the family's means test?

sides.answer: Yes. A benefit measured on the household measures both incomes.
No. The second income becomes the reason the first is refused.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The incumbent-hedging question. REF 8.1 recovers campaign questions from the American material; the recovered pool contains no question about the timing advantage of the party already in office.
cards.question: Should the ruling party campaign on the day the budget is presented?

sides.answer: Yes. Six weeks of undivided attention beats one week of it.
No. On the day it lands, the number is already the story.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.1 item 5 is the only recovered question about spending, and it asks about space. This asks about the ordinary recurring purchase every district makes, where visibility and price pull in opposite directions.
cards.question: Should the district's advertising contract go to the highest bidder?

sides.answer: Yes. The highest bidder has at least proved it can pay.
No. The highest bidder is on every hoarding for a decade.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The land question. ig-in2020-016 asks whether land records should be digitised; nothing in the recovered pool asks what happens to the ground once they are.
cards.question: Should a new industrial corridor be built through the fields or the city?

sides.answer: Yes. The city already has the buyers and the trucks.
No. The fields are the only thing here that was not built.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The inter-generational question, which the recovered pool has no instance of at all: every recovered card decides something inside one electoral term.
cards.question: Should the next gas block be opened before the current one is empty?

sides.answer: Yes. The block is licensed, the wells are surveyed, the gas is sold.
No. A block opened early is a field emptied two years early.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Transparency with a price on it. The Capitalist side is the one that votes to keep a file closed, so the question does not reward the reflex of its own answer.
cards.question: Should the procurement portal be open to anyone who asks for a file?

sides.answer: No. Bidder names are worth more than the files holding them.
Yes. A portal nobody reads is a cabinet with a firewall.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Extends the procurement family of ig-in2020-013 and ig-in2020-014 from the price of the work to the name on the envelope.
cards.question: Should a large contractor bid using a local partner's name?

sides.answer: Yes. The consortium is what the tender was written for.
No. The name is the whole bid, and the name was not theirs.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Both sides here are defensible and neither is cheap, which is the register's ordinary shape: two spends competing for one season.
cards.question: Should the border road be built before the flood relief is finished?

sides.answer: Yes. A road that cannot be flooded is worth two seasons.
No. The relief is this year, and the road is also this year.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Sovereignty against cost. The Capitalist side is the one that opens the tender to a foreign firm, so the greedy reading of the Ideologue and the cautious reading coincide on this card.
cards.question: Should a foreign firm be allowed to bid for a national port?

sides.answer: Yes. Whoever builds it fastest also builds it cheapest.
No. A port is an address, and an address can be changed.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Disclosure of a number that the state controls. The recovered pool contains no question about a published statistic, which is the ordinary instrument of the register.
cards.question: Should the district hospital publish its death rate every quarter?

sides.answer: Yes. A number that is published is one somebody answers for.
No. A quarterly number is a quarterly campaign for whoever it hurts.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Eligibility rather than existence. ig-in2020-017 asks whether a scheme should reach further geographically; this asks whether it should be universal or means-tested, which is the same money for a different named group.
cards.question: Should free travel serve everyone or only those who cannot pay?

sides.answer: Yes. Everyone, and the fare is what pays for everyone else.
No. Those who can pay, and the scheme stays legible from a bus.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Language policy. Neither recovered welfare question nor any of the eight recovered stems asks who has to be addressed in what language to receive a benefit.
cards.question: Should the state's message be issued in the states' own languages?

sides.answer: Yes. A message nobody reads in the first hour is issued twice.
No. One message, one spokesperson, and one number to correct.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Extends the transparency family of ig-in2020-016 and ig-in2020-041 from records to money actually moved, and both sides agree the deadline is correct and disagree about whether it has force.
cards.question: Should every transfer to a panchayat be published within a month?

sides.answer: Yes. Published in a month, spent and accounted for.
No. Published in a month, read in a quarter, disputed in a year.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Two constituencies with incompatible reasons, which is the register's preferred shape: both sides are defending somebody, neither is defending a self-interest.
cards.question: Should the pension fund be lent to a new manufacturing scheme?

sides.answer: Yes. A factory that employs people funds their pensions better.
No. The fund is the only promise kept fifty years without a vote.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Borders. REF 2.3 [INFERRED] that Idealist and Supremo sit in largely disjoint question space, and ig-in2020-001 and ig-in2020-032 already touch the seam; this is the fourth card on it and the first that asks who an administrative line is drawn for.
cards.question: Should the state border be redrawn where the people live?

sides.answer: Yes. A line that ignores a village produces two governments for it.
No. The line is the one thing everyone agreed on at the start.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. An unprofitable service. The recovered pool has no question about whether to keep running something that loses money, which is the ordinary form of most state expenditure.
cards.question: Should loss-making public transport be kept running or written off?

sides.answer: Yes. A bus on a losing route is the only seat some people have.
No. A service with no fare has no driver and a road has no police.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The courts. REF 8.1 recovers no institutional question at all, and a deadline imposed on an institution that does not control its backlog is the register's sharpest ordinary dilemma.
cards.question: Should the courts be told to clear all pending cases this year?

sides.answer: Yes. Clear them, and the reason for the delay becomes visible.
No. A clearance order moves the queue and keeps the count.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Broadcast form as a question. The recovered Showstopper questions are all about whether to say something; this one is about where it is said, which the cut decides for you.
cards.question: Should the television debate come from one studio or two?

sides.answer: Yes. One room, and the clip that circulates is the exchange.
No. Two rooms, and no single cut can be called the debate.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Internal party discipline. Extends ig-in2020-037 from the calendar advantage of the incumbent to whether its own members are countable in public, which is a different institutional question.
cards.question: Should the ruling party's internal vote be shown to the public?

sides.answer: Yes. Show it, and the next election is a count rather than a campaign.
No. A party that counts itself in public cannot revise a number.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The distribution question that every recovered card abstains from: not whether to build something but which district it goes in. The Showstopper side is the one arguing for the minister's own district, so the patronage reading is not automatically the greedy side.
cards.question: Should the minister's own district get the new hospital?

sides.answer: Yes. The district asked for it and the minister has seen the file.
No. A hospital in the minister's district is a poster with beds.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. A one-month bilateral concession, which is the register's preferred shape: both sides can be defended, and the disagreement is entirely about what a precedent is worth.
cards.question: Should the border open to pilgrims without a visa for one month?

sides.answer: Yes. Open it, and the month is photographed from both sides.
No. Open it once, and it becomes the standing arrangement.
